ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a sheet of grid paper, on which there are six black marked points. Taking a grid intersection in the upper left as the origin, rightward as the positive x direction, and downward as the positive y direction, the six points can be read according to the integer grid, for example A=(6,1), B=(3,2), C=(7,2), D=(1,4), E=(5,4), F=(3,6). Reasoning: Using these points, the listed common figures can be constructed. The side vectors of D-B-E-F are successively (2,-2), (2,2), (-2,2), (-2,-2); the four sides are equal in length and the dot product of adjacent sides is 0, so it is a square; therefore under the usual inclusive definition, it can also be used as a rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram, kite, or general quadrilateral. In B-C-E-D, BC and DE are parallel and equal in length, and CE and DB are parallel and equal in length, so a non-rectangular parallelogram can be formed. If a trapezoid with strictly only one pair of parallel sides is needed, in A-C-E-B the direction of AC is (1,1), and the direction of EB is (-2,-2); the two are parallel, while the other pair of sides is not parallel, so a trapezoid can be formed. A triangle can take any three non-collinear points, such as A, B, C. From these constructions it can be seen that all the listed figures can be drawn using points among the six marked points as vertices.

Image description: The figure is a sheet of grid paper, on which there are six black marked points. Taking a grid intersection in the upper left as the origin, rightward as the positive x direction, and downward as the positive y direction, the six points can be read according to the integer grid, for example A=(6,1), B=(3,2), C=(7,2), D=(1,4), E=(5,4), F=(3,6).
Reasoning: Using these points, the listed common figures can be constructed. The side vectors of D-B-E-F are successively (2,-2), (2,2), (-2,2), (-2,-2); the four sides are equal in length and the dot product of adjacent sides is 0, so it is a square; therefore under the usual inclusive definition, it can also be used as a rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram, kite, or general quadrilateral. In B-C-E-D, BC and DE are parallel and equal in length, and CE and DB are parallel and equal in length, so a non-rectangular parallelogram can be formed. If a trapezoid with strictly only one pair of parallel sides is needed, in A-C-E-B the direction of AC is (1,1), and the direction of EB is (-2,-2); the two are parallel, while the other pair of sides is not parallel, so a trapezoid can be formed. A triangle can take any three non-collinear points, such as A, B, C. From these constructions it can be seen that all the listed figures can be drawn using points among the six marked points as vertices.
